must_include: The abstract reports 18,420 firm-year observations from 2004–2022.
The main result is stated as a 0.8 percentage-point association with a 95% confidence interval of 0.3 to 1.3 percentage points.
The 12.4% mean is used as an economic benchmark without changing the unit of the estimate.
The financing-risk evidence is described as suggestive rather than definitive.
The consistency note explicitly resolves the 1.2-versus-0.8 conflict, causal language, and universal-scope claim.
must_avoid: Causal verbs that imply the descriptive design identifies an effect.
Any invented citation, test, coefficient, sample restriction, or mechanism result.
Claims that the association holds for every firm.
Presenting the unrated-firm split as proof of financing risk.
human_review: The same authoritative magnitude, unit, and scope appear throughout the response.
The prose is readable as manuscript text rather than an evaluator checklist.
